assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and the Jarzynski and Crooks relations are exact results for systems driven arbitrarily far from equilibrium, linking work distributions to equilibrium free-energy differences and giving the second law a precise statistical meaning. They are conceptually original, clean and widely used in stochastic thermodynamics, single-molecule pulling experiments and simulation methods. From a statistical-physics viewpoint this is the strongest fundamental-theory candidate on the list.
assessment.attribution: Jarzynski (equality, 1997) and Crooks (detailed fluctuation relation, 1999) are the clearest decisive contributors. Evans and collaborators (Evans-Cohen-Morriss, Evans-Searles) have a strong claim for the early fluctuation theorem; Gallavotti and Cohen are not in the supplied credit, so the full history cannot be represented. I propose the three supplied names and flag the incompleteness.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed for over two decades (RNA hairpin unfolding, colloidal particles, small quantum and electronic systems), with stable interpretation and broad uptake. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority among the Evans-Searles, Gallavotti-Cohen, Jarzynski and Crooks lines is a long-standing question and some key figures are not in the credited names.
I rely on my own knowledge of the history and have not verified individual dates here.
Whether the prize is judged mainly a theory prize or needs experimental emphasis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new class of quantum matter with protected edge and surface states, tied to deep mathematical structure and with consequences across condensed-matter physics. The quantum spin Hall prediction and observation and the three-dimensional materials form a coherent, well-understood narrative. Importance and originality are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal of the Z2 invariant and quantum spin Hall state; Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposed HgTe, realized by Molenkamp's group; Hasan led the first three-dimensional observations. Mele is a co-author of the founding Kane-Mele work and a fair claim, and Bernevig, Zhang, Fu and Moore are outside the supplied names. I choose Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan as the best three-person configuration supported by the credit list, recognizing that Mele's omission is awkward.
assessment.maturity: Mature: independent confirmations in HgTe, Bi-based and other materials, ARPES and transport, for roughly two decades. The 2016 prize recognized topological phase transitions but not this specific discovery, so the topic remains open.
uncertainties: Credit is split among theory (Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Zhang, Fu, Moore) and experiment, so any three-person selection leaves out strong contributors.
Overlap with the 2016 prize and with candidate B003 requires care.
I am relying on memory for the roles of individual groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices made it possible to realize Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters and to observe the superfluid-Mott insulator transition and, later, single-site resolved many-body dynamics. This is a clear route to controlled analog quantum simulation of many-body and statistical-physics problems, with lasting influence on the study of nonequilibrium and strongly correlated systems.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and coworkers (with Jaksch, Cirac and others) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realization; Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott transition experiment (2002) and subsequent quantum gas microscopy developments. Cirac is also credited and is a strong theorist but is not selected, so a three-person group of Bloch, Greiner and Zoller is the most coherent. Hänsch and Jaksch contributions are not represented.
assessment.maturity: Strong, independently confirmed by many groups for over twenty years; the field is mature, though the scientific payoff of simulation is still developing. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Overlap with Cirac-Zoller trapped-ion and atomic quantum-information candidates may make the allocation awkward.
Whether the key discovery is the Mott transition experiment or the broader simulation program is not settled by the supplied text.
Quantum advantage over classical simulation remains an open question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, based on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and prospects for a redefinition of the second. This is a clear, high-impact invention with direct metrological and fundamental-physics significance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock; Ye's group pushed performance to the current record. Two names fit the credit list well and give a clean, uncontested allocation. Hall and Hänsch already received a share in 2005 for frequency combs, which the clocks build on.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many laboratories (JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST, SYRTE). Mature and still improving; recognition could be timely, though a formal redefinition of the second is not yet done.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to wait for the redefinition of the second.
Possible overlap in the committee's mind with earlier time-and-frequency prizes.
Contributions from ion-clock groups are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos by IceCube and the later association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane opened a new messenger in astronomy. It required a technical invention on a large scale (the Antarctic ice Cherenkov detector) and delivers lasting scientific results.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Karle is a leading figure in its design and analysis, which gives a compact two-person credit. Because IceCube is a large collaboration with leaders and early AMANDA contributions, the supplied two-name configuration is somewhat narrow and might be contested.
assessment.maturity: The 2013 discovery is independently supported by multiple analyses, though the astrophysical sources of most of the flux are still not identified. Reasonably mature as a discovery, partly premature as an interpretation.
uncertainties: Sources of the diffuse flux are not fully understood, so the astrophysics interpretation could change.
Allocation of credit within a large collaboration is disputed.
My assessment of the history is from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experiments on strongly interacting Fermi gases tuned through a Feshbach resonance explored the BCS-BEC crossover, universal thermodynamics, and superfluidity in a controllable system, serving as a model for strongly correlated matter including neutron stars and cuprates. Scientific value is high, particularly for universality and many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Grimm and Salomon led molecular BEC and crossover experiments, with Ketterle and Jin also central; Deborah Jin is deceased and not in the credit list. Ketterle is already a laureate (2001), so I propose Grimm and Salomon; this is a defensible but incomplete allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed, but credit is dispersed over many groups and years, and the discovery is arguably a research program rather than a single result.
uncertainties: The decisive contributors are shared with a deceased researcher and an existing laureate.
It may be viewed as incremental after the 2001 prize for BEC.
Whether to choose a single observation or a field is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene revealed correlated insulators and superconductivity in a simple, tunable moire platform and initiated twistronics. The theory prediction of flat bands at a magic angle followed by dramatic experiments is a striking combination, and the field has expanded greatly.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands (2011); Jarillo-Herrero's group demonstrated correlated states and superconductivity (2018). Cao and coworkers who did the experiments are not credited. This theory-plus-experiment pairing is clear, though Cao's role is a concern.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups since 2018, but the nature of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still being debated. Fairly young, so may be premature.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Missing credited names (e.g. Yuan Cao, Pablo's collaborators).
Reproducibility across samples and twist-angle disorder.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic oscillation feature gives a calibrated standard ruler in the galaxy distribution and has become a cornerstone of precision cosmology, constraining dark energy and the expansion history. It is a clean physical effect with robust measurements.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein and collaborators detected the peak in SDSS luminous red galaxies (2005), and Cole, Peacock and the 2dFGRS team independently reported it; theory contributions (Peebles-Yu, Sunyaev-Zeldovich) are not in the credit. The three names support a plausible prize configuration but attribution is partly arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by SDSS, 2dF, BOSS, DESI and others; well established. Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy may refine interpretation but not the detection.
uncertainties: Theory origin predates the observations and is not credited.
Large-collaboration credit among SDSS and 2dF teams.
This lies outside my own field, so I weight it by general importance only.
